newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, US agree that demand-led growth important.
newsitem.headline: Japan, US agree that demand-led growth important.

text.p: Japan and the United States agreed on Friday that domestic demand-led growth was important for each country, and that it was important that Japan's trade surplus did not expand drastically, Japanese officials told reporters.
The officials were speaking after U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin met Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
Japanese government officials quoted Hashimoto as telling Rubin that Japan's trade surplus was unlikely grow drastically as a general trend.

Hashimoto also said that there may be some impact on the economy from the increase in consumption tax to five percent from three percent this month. However, spillover from the extra budget for the fiscal year just ended, should help support the economy in the April to June period, the officials quoted Hashimoto as saying.
The two did not discuss foreign exchange or issues related to fiscal restructuring, the officials said.
Rubin made no specific policy demands on Japan, the officials said.
The officials said Hashimoto explained the recent restructuring measures for domestic banks.
Hashimoto said that aggressive deregulation measures, including financial system reform, would be positive for the Japanese economy. Rubin nodded in agreement to this, the officials said.
